label: folio-assistant vocabulary (harness only)
comment: Every class and property the folio knowledge graph projects, one node each. Generated by scripts/ns-export.ts; graph-kind definitions are read from the declaration registry rather than restated here.

@graph.label: FshGutsNode
@graph.comment: One item in the trashcan: something deprecated or thrown away, kept and addressable rather than deleted, and deliberately absent from the rendered site. Carries where it used to live, so it is not an orphan.
@graph.definition: One item in the trashcan: something deprecated or thrown away, kept and addressable rather than deleted, and deliberately absent from the rendered site. Carries where it used to live, so it is not an orphan.

@graph.label: Instance
@graph.comment: A repository carrying a harness declaration — it names itself, its published stub, and the directories it holds.
@graph.definition: A repository carrying a harness declaration — it names itself, its published stub, and the directories it holds.

@graph.label: Folio
@graph.comment: A repository that authors folio content — it declares a content type, and `folio_init` wrote its config. Distinct from an Instance: this repository's `cat-harness/` is an Instance and is not a Folio.
@graph.definition: A repository that authors folio content — it declares a content type, and `folio_init` wrote its config. Distinct from an Instance: this repository's `cat-harness/` is an Instance and is not a Folio.

@graph.label: SushiProject
@graph.comment: A repository SUSHI will build — FSH compiled to a FHIR implementation guide. Minted here because SUSHI publishes no logical model for its own config; this is our name for the membership, not a claim to define SUSHI.
@graph.definition: A repository SUSHI will build — FSH compiled to a FHIR implementation guide. Minted here because SUSHI publishes no logical model for its own config; this is our name for the membership, not a claim to define SUSHI.

@graph.label: Convention
@graph.comment: A standing rule an actor must hold while performing a task, bound to a process, a lane or an activity rather than loaded unconditionally. Resolution is first-binding-wins along that order, not a merge, so a reader asking why a rule applies here gets one answer.
@graph.definition: A standing rule an actor must hold while performing a task, bound to a process, a lane or an activity rather than loaded unconditionally. Resolution is first-binding-wins along that order, not a merge, so a reader asking why a rule applies here gets one answer.

@graph.label: Requirement
@graph.comment: A stated need a change must satisfy, elicited and signed off in the CRDM process before implementation begins. Distinct from the issue that tracks it and the bean that plans the work.
@graph.definition: A stated need a change must satisfy, elicited and signed off in the CRDM process before implementation begins. Distinct from the issue that tracks it and the bean that plans the work.

@graph.label: LaneUsage
@graph.comment: One appearance of a glossary concept as a swimlane in one BPMN process — the process it is in, the label that process gave the lane, and that lane's own documentation. A usage is an occurrence, not a term: it is regenerated wholesale and never retired, while a concept is a term somebody may have cited.
@graph.definition: One appearance of a glossary concept as a swimlane in one BPMN process — the process it is in, the label that process gave the lane, and that lane's own documentation. A usage is an occurrence, not a term: it is regenerated wholesale and never retired, while a concept is a term somebody may have cited.

@graph.label: SkillPackage
@graph.comment: A directory of skills shipped and versioned together.
@graph.definition: A directory of skills shipped and versioned together.

@graph.label: Tool
@graph.comment: A callable operation the harness exposes, declared as a node rather than only as code.
@graph.definition: A callable operation the harness exposes, declared as a node rather than only as code.

@graph.label: Schema
@graph.comment: A schema definition, itself a node in the knowledge graph rather than an island beside one.
@graph.definition: A schema definition, itself a node in the knowledge graph rather than an island beside one.

@graph.label: Capability
@graph.comment: Something an actor's environment provides — a binary, a service, a credential — probed rather than assumed.
@graph.definition: Something an actor's environment provides — a binary, a service, a credential — probed rather than assumed.

@graph.label: Harness
@graph.comment: An instance's root declaration: the directories it scans and the graphs they hold.
@graph.definition: An instance's root declaration: the directories it scans and the graphs they hold.

@graph.label: RoleGraph
@graph.comment: The role registry as a graph — every role, what it inherits, and the lanes it binds.
@graph.definition: The role registry as a graph — every role, what it inherits, and the lanes it binds.

@graph.label: BeanDefsGraph
@graph.comment: Work items — one Markdown file each, in the layout the `beans` CLI reads. Authored and edited by people and agents.
@graph.definition: Work items — one Markdown file each, in the layout the `beans` CLI reads. Authored and edited by people and agents.

@graph.label: BeanGraph
@graph.comment: The work plan — what is being worked on, and where each running BPMN instance got to. Its inner directories are declared by `beans/beans.json`.
@graph.definition: The work plan — what is being worked on, and where each running BPMN instance got to. Its inner directories are declared by `beans/beans.json`.

@graph.label: BoardGraph
@graph.comment: Boards — one JSON file each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-board/v1"`. A board is a diagram OF a folio: it declares what it shows, and a folio with no board is complete. Schema: `schemas/board.ts`.
@graph.definition: Boards — one JSON file each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-board/v1"`. A board is a diagram OF a folio: it declares what it shows, and a folio with no board is complete. Schema: `schemas/board.ts`.

@graph.label: BoardPositionsGraph
@graph.comment: Where each note sits on each board — `board-positions.json`, keyed by board then by note id, in board units. The layout layer, which points at notes and is never pointed back at. Schema: `schemas/board-positions.ts`.
@graph.definition: Where each note sits on each board — `board-positions.json`, keyed by board then by note id, in board units. The layout layer, which points at notes and is never pointed back at. Schema: `schemas/board-positions.ts`.

@graph.label: CatalogueGraph
@graph.comment: A remote catalogue modelled by reference — communities, collections and items of a corpus the instance does not hold. Every node declares whether its bytes are here (`materialized`), elsewhere (`referenced`) or unestablished (`unknown`), with no default. Distinct from `library`, which is content that IS here.
@graph.definition: A remote catalogue modelled by reference — communities, collections and items of a corpus the instance does not hold. Every node declares whether its bytes are here (`materialized`), elsewhere (`referenced`) or unestablished (`unknown`), with no default. Distinct from `library`, which is content that IS here.

@graph.label: DocsGraph
@graph.comment: Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph — how the harness works, what its directories hold, how a process runs. Rendered by the plain just-the-docs pipeline. Distinct from `folio`, which is content an author CREATES using the graph; the difference is the SUBJECT, not the format. The who-iris catalogue is `library/`; a note about it is a `folio`; the page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`.
@graph.definition: Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph — how the harness works, what its directories hold, how a process runs. Rendered by the plain just-the-docs pipeline. Distinct from `folio`, which is content an author CREATES using the graph; the difference is the SUBJECT, not the format. The who-iris catalogue is `library/`; a note about it is a `folio`; the page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`.

@graph.label: FhirArtifactIndexGraph
@graph.comment: The artefact index of a published FHIR Implementation Guide, reconstructed from its published output — every artefact by canonical URL and published representation, with the DAK API's JSON Schema / JSON-LD sidecars as an overlay where the IG publishes one. No IG publishes such an index itself, so every field records which file it came out of.
@graph.definition: The artefact index of a published FHIR Implementation Guide, reconstructed from its published output — every artefact by canonical URL and published representation, with the DAK API's JSON Schema / JSON-LD sidecars as an overlay where the IG publishes one. No IG publishes such an index itself, so every field records which file it came out of.

@graph.label: FshGutsGraph
@graph.comment: Deprecated and throwaway structured content — kept, addressable and exported, and deliberately absent from the rendered site. The destination for anything that would otherwise be deleted, and for SDLC churn that must not reach the folio's readers.
@graph.definition: Deprecated and throwaway structured content — kept, addressable and exported, and deliberately absent from the rendered site. The destination for anything that would otherwise be deleted, and for SDLC churn that must not reach the folio's readers.

@graph.label: GlossaryGraph
@graph.comment: The swimlane glossary's retirement ledger — every concept this instance has ever minted, with the date it was first seen and the date it stopped being derivable. Written by scripts/glossary-export.ts; the glossary document itself is derived and not stored here.
@graph.definition: The swimlane glossary's retirement ledger — every concept this instance has ever minted, with the date it was first seen and the date it stopped being derivable. Written by scripts/glossary-export.ts; the glossary document itself is derived and not stored here.

@graph.label: HealthGraph
@graph.comment: Repository health reports — one `health-report/v1` document per sweep, carrying every check's three-state verdict, the thresholds it applied and the basis each threshold was chosen on. Generated by `test/health/run.ts`; never hand-edited.
@graph.definition: Repository health reports — one `health-report/v1` document per sweep, carrying every check's three-state verdict, the thresholds it applied and the basis each threshold was chosen on. Generated by `test/health/run.ts`; never hand-edited.

@graph.label: InteractionGraph
@graph.comment: How a person wants to be asked — read at session start, never written by a process.
@graph.definition: How a person wants to be asked — read at session start, never written by a process.

@graph.label: IssueMarkGraph
@graph.comment: How far an agent has read an issue — the comment id and the edit time it accounted for.
@graph.definition: How far an agent has read an issue — the comment id and the edit time it accounted for.

@graph.label: MemoryGraph
@graph.comment: Durable facts an agent carries between sessions. Read during a process, never written by one.
@graph.definition: Durable facts an agent carries between sessions. Read during a process, never written by one.

@graph.label: MethodologyGraph
@graph.comment: Judgement methodologies, adopted whole and kept independent — parallel ways to reach a decision, selected by context.
@graph.definition: Judgement methodologies, adopted whole and kept independent — parallel ways to reach a decision, selected by context.

@graph.label: ProcessGraph
@graph.comment: Executable BPMN processes and the DMN tables their gateways compute from.
@graph.definition: Executable BPMN processes and the DMN tables their gateways compute from.

@graph.label: QaGraph
@graph.comment: QA witnesses — one `qa-witness/v1` document per audited subject, in three families (`block`, `kg`, `translation`), projected for the docs site from the verdicts that live beside their subjects. Generated; never hand-edited.
@graph.definition: QA witnesses — one `qa-witness/v1` document per audited subject, in three families (`block`, `kg`, `translation`), projected for the docs site from the verdicts that live beside their subjects. Generated; never hand-edited.

@graph.label: ScenarioGraph
@graph.comment: Actors, the Roles they take on, and the User Stories those Roles serve.
@graph.definition: Actors, the Roles they take on, and the User Stories those Roles serve.

@graph.label: SessionStateGraph
@graph.comment: A session's context — the acting actor, the instances it has open, and what it waits on.
@graph.definition: A session's context — the acting actor, the instances it has open, and what it waits on.

@graph.label: SkillGraph
@graph.comment: Skill packages — the authored instruction bodies an Actor performs a Task from.
@graph.definition: Skill packages — the authored instruction bodies an Actor performs a Task from.

@graph.label: ThemeGraph
@graph.comment: Themes derived from an instance's own sources — one Theme node each, carrying `kind: sticky | webpage | publication`. The palette vocabulary is shared across every kind and only the geometry varies; every value cites where it was measured.
@graph.definition: Themes derived from an instance's own sources — one Theme node each, carrying `kind: sticky | webpage | publication`. The palette vocabulary is shared across every kind and only the geometry varies; every value cites where it was measured.

@graph.label: ToolGraph
@graph.comment: Tool definitions — themselves nodes in the KG, per the repo taxonomy.
@graph.definition: Tool definitions — themselves nodes in the KG, per the repo taxonomy.

@graph.label: TranslationSourceGraph
@graph.comment: POT templates, PO catalogues and their `TranslationNode` manifests, one directory per target locale. The INPUT to injection; the rendered output is ordinary content that declares its own `lang`.
@graph.definition: POT templates, PO catalogues and their `TranslationNode` manifests, one directory per target locale. The INPUT to injection; the rendered output is ordinary content that declares its own `lang`.

@graph.label: WaiverGraph
@graph.comment: Confirmations a person granted in advance — each naming one gate, scoped to a session or a process run, each expiring.
@graph.definition: Confirmations a person granted in advance — each naming one gate, scoped to a session or a process run, each expiring.

@graph.label: WorkflowStateGraph
@graph.comment: Running BPMN instances — one JSON file each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-workflow-instance/v1"`. Owned by the interpreter, never hand-edited.
@graph.definition: Running BPMN instances — one JSON file each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-workflow-instance/v1"`. Owned by the interpreter, never hand-edited.

@graph.label: partOf
@graph.comment: The node this one belongs to.
@graph.definition: The node this one belongs to.

@graph.label: inPackage

@graph.definition: The skill package a skill ships in.

@graph.label: inSubgraph
@graph.comment: The DECLARED DIRECTORY a node was projected from — the named subgraph it belongs to, as a link to that directory's own node rather than a bare id. Derived from the instance's declaration, longest path prefix winning, and INHERITED through `partOf` for nodes that have no path of their own (a ProcessNode is part of a diagram, not a file). A node with no value belongs to no declared directory — vocabulary nodes are minted from the namespace rather than from any file — and that absence is reported as its own state rather than folded into a default.
@graph.definition: The DECLARED DIRECTORY a node was projected from — the named subgraph it belongs to, as a link to that directory's own node rather than a bare id. @graph.definition: The node's own identifier within its file, before any IRI is minted.

@graph.definition: The source module a node was projected from.

@graph.definition: What a declared asset is FOR, as the instance names it — `instance-readme`, `agent-instructions`. A literal, and not the swimlane Role, which is a node with skills.

@graph.definition: The IRI of a node's type, so a consumer need not parse the `@type` string.

@graph.label: statement
@graph.comment: What a convention REQUIRES, in one line. Distinct from rdfs:comment, which is prose about the node: this is the rule itself, and a consumer filtering for enforceable text needs the two apart.
@graph.definition: What a convention REQUIRES, in one line. Distinct from rdfs:comment, which is prose about the node: this is the rule itself, and a consumer filtering for enforceable text needs the two apart.

@graph.label: rationale
@graph.comment: Why a convention holds, so a reader can tell whether it still does. Kept separate from the statement deliberately — a rule and its justification collapsed into one field is a rule nobody can retire, because nothing is left that says what would falsify it.
@graph.definition: Why a convention holds, so a reader can tell whether it still does. Kept separate from the statement deliberately — a rule and its justification collapsed into one field is a rule nobody can retire, because nothing is left that says what would falsify it.

@graph.label: applies
@graph.comment: The surfaces a convention governs — `typescript`, `bpmn`, `commit-message`. A filter, not prose, and open rather than enumerated: a closed set would have to be edited before a convention about a new surface could exist.
@graph.definition: The surfaces a convention governs — `typescript`, `bpmn`, `commit-message`. A filter, not prose, and open rather than enumerated: a closed set would have to be edited before a convention about a new surface could exist.
